The '''2002 World Championship''' was the 7th Star Wars CCG World Championship and the first run by the [[Players Committee]]. It was played at [[DecipherCon 2002]] at the Chesapeake Conference Center from 31 October to 3 November 2002.<ref name="dcon-fmt">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020810223927/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/events/worldsformats.html World Championship Event Formats & Prizes] (Wayback, 10 August 2002)</ref><ref name="tfn">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/World_Championship_Results_announced_64778.asp World Championship Results announced], theforce.net (3 November 2002)</ref><ref name="pc-sw">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021221153832/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/1103swyjjkresults.html Star Wars Players Committee 2002 World Championships], Kathy McCracken, Decipher Daily News (3 November 2002)</ref> The Players Committee's awards page gives the site as "DecipherCon – Virginia Beach, VA".<ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org; Wayback [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222457/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ 17 August 2023]</ref> [[Angelo Consoli]] of Germany won with a Dark [[No Money, No Parts, No Deal! / You're A Slave?|No Money, No Parts, No Deal!]] (Watto) deck and a Light [[Quiet Mining Colony / Independent Operation|Quiet Mining Colony]] deck, beating [[Greg Shaw]] in a final that ended at 5:30 AM on Sunday.<ref name="tfn" /><ref name="pc-sw" /><ref name="d4">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030220124438/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/1103dayfourwrapup.html Until Next Time: Day Four Wrapup], Marcus Sheppard, Decipher Daily News (3 November 2002)</ref> The purse was $10,000.<ref name="dcon-fmt" /> The two Day 1 heats drew 45 and 54 players, and Day 2 had 52 players: 20 who qualified at DecipherCon and 32 who qualified on the Road to Worlds.<ref name="pc-dconwrap" /> Duane Bruun's year-end article for the Players Committee gives 99 Day 1 players in total and 54 on Day 2.<ref name="pc-bruun02">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030613110815/http://swccgpc.com:80/News/duane2002yearend.htm The State Of SWCCG], Duane Bruun (PC Staff Writer), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 13 June 2003.</ref>

The constructed pool was [[Premiere - Original VS3]]: printed sets through [[Theed Palace]] plus original virtual cards through [[Virtual Set 3: Revolution|VS3]] (legal 20 September 2002).

Places 1–2 as announced at the Sunday awards by [[Jim Colson]]; places 3–8 in the order the Players Committee published afterwards.<ref name="tfn" /><ref name="pc-sw" /><ref name="pc-dconwrap" /> Decks are the lists recovered in 2026 from DeckTech posts (Internet Archive copies) and Players Committee decklist forms; each deck page cites its own source. Prizes are from Decipher's event page.<ref name="dcon-fmt" />

The Sunday awards announced places 3–4 and 5–8 as ties.<ref name="pc-nov02">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030423221953/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/november02archives.htm November Updates (2002)], Josh Radke (3 November 2002), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 23 April 2003.</ref> The Players Committee's wrap-up by Tournament Support Advocate [[Andrew Howard]] then listed the final standings "with tiebreaks determined according to placement from the swiss rounds": 3rd Brian Fred (Indiana), 4th Brian Terwilliger (New York), 5th Hayes Hunter (Massachusetts/Arizona), 6th Jonathan Chu (Tennessee), 7th Brian Rippetoe (Tennessee) and 8th Bastian Winkelhaus (Germany); it gives Consoli's home as Germany and Shaw's as New Jersey.<ref name="pc-dconwrap" /> A 2020 forum compilation lists [[Clint Hays]] in place of Hayes Hunter among 5th–8th; a reply in the same thread corrects it to Hayes Hunter, as in the official results.<ref name="f75427-1300387">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1300387#p1300387 Post by Yoshi], "SWCCG Worlds Day 3 Standings History", forum.starwarsccg.org (28 May 2020). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20211006195438/https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=75427 Internet Archive], [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012152200/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t75427.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="f75427-1300392">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1300392#p1300392 Post by Death Star], "SWCCG Worlds Day 3 Standings History", forum.starwarsccg.org (28 May 2020). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20211006195438/https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=75427 Internet Archive], [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012152200/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t75427.html Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Top 8 bracket ===

The top 8 played single elimination from 6:00 PM on Saturday 2 November; the final ended at 5:30 AM on Sunday 3 November.<ref name="pc-sw" /><ref name="d4" /> The top 8 in Swiss order after Day 2 were Angelo Consoli, Hayes Hunter, Jonathan Chu, Brian Fred, Brian Rippetoe, Greg Shaw, Brian Terwilliger and Bastian Winkelhaus. The Players Committee's wrap-up says the finals "began around 9-10pm, and ended at approximately 5:30am".<ref name="pc-dconwrap" /> The quarterfinal and semifinal pairings and game results were not published in the sources found.

=== Schedule ===

Two Day 1 heats ran on Thursday 31 October and Friday 1 November at 2:00 PM: six games of Swiss, with the top 20% advancing to Day 2. Day 2 on Saturday 2 November started at 10:00 AM.<ref name="swsched">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021023190505/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/events/eventschedule-otherccg.html Event schedule: Star Wars, Young Jedi, Jedi Knights], Decipher (Wayback 23 October 2002)</ref><ref name="tfn-sched">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Star_Wars_CCG_Explodes_at_DecipherCon_2002_65230.asp Star Wars CCG Explodes at DecipherCon 2002], theforce.net (20 September 2002)</ref><ref name="pc-sw" /> Day 2 was eight rounds of Swiss before the cut to the top 8.<ref name="pc-dconwrap" /> No full Day 1 or Day 2 standings have been found; the Day 1 qualifiers are listed below.

== Day 1 ==

Two Day 1 heats qualified the top 20% for Day 2. Day 1A on Thursday 31 October had 45 players and 9 qualifiers; Day 1B on Friday 1 November had 54 players and 11 qualifiers. The qualifiers are listed in placement order. Other players in Day 1A included [[Mat Allen]], [[Don Kitzman]], [[Tim Guzman]] and [[Michael Dalton]]; Hideki Matsumoto travelled from Japan to play. [[Yannick Lapointe]] attended on Friday.<ref name="pc-dconwrap" />

== Side events ==

The Players Committee's wrap-up gives these other events and attendances:<ref name="pc-dconwrap" />

* Friday 1 November: Jedi Knights Super Sealed Deck (8 players), Young Jedi Secret Squirrel (8), Star Wars Death Star II/Endor booster draft (8), Star Wars Highlander (4) and Star Wars Secret Squirrel (14).
* Friday night: a non-sanctioned playtest tournament for the new Classic Format, run by [[Scott Lingrell]]. [[Drew Scott]] won it and $35. See [[Classic]].
* Saturday 2 November: Star Wars Special Edition booster draft (10 players) and a Star Wars "A New Hope" theme tournament (4), plus the Jedi Knights World Championship (23 players) and the Young Jedi World Championship (28 players).

The Young Jedi and Jedi Knights results were announced with the Star Wars places at the Sunday awards. Young Jedi: 1st [[Jason Kilby|Jason Killby]] ($500 and trophy), 2nd Jeremy Baker, 3rd Dale Hanak, 4th Vincent Serret. Jedi Knights: 1st [[Jeff Kahan|Jeffrey Kahan]] ($500 and trophy), 2nd Justin Beal, 3rd Brian Muller, 4th Bradford Bedlion.<ref name="pc-nov02" />
